I will do it the way I know can hold yield and not gamble too much. My land is 14.5 mu, wheat after maize, maize after wheat, same ground turning over all year. I have done this a long time, so I do not start from empty talk, I start from what usually works here. If I cut fertilizer too hard and the crop turns weak, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. So I will feed both crops solidly, but not foolishly. I will use the kinds of seed I have seen do well around me. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, because these years the better ones stand better and fill grain better than the old seed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here that is what gives ears and yield. I have well water, so I will not let the crop sit thirsty if the sky does not help.

For wheat, I will put more strength at the start and then add more nitrogen when it starts pulling up in spring. I will plough or rotary it well after maize, get the seedbed even, sow on time, and give about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu over the season. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if dry, once at spring jointing, and once around grain filling if needed. I will spray about 2 times, mostly watching for weeds first and then disease or aphids if they show. If the season behaves, I will look for around 550 kg per mu.

For maize, I will move fast after wheat harvest. I do not like losing moisture and time, so I will mostly go no-tillage or very light disturbance, then seed hybrid maize straight in. Maize eats fertilizer hard, so I will give about 14 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu, with a good part of the nitrogen going when the plants get tall, not all dumped at once. I will water about 2 times in a normal year, one around seedling establishment if dry and one around big flare or silking. I will spray about 2 times, mainly for weeds early and then for armyworm, corn borer, or leaf disease if I see pressure. If nothing goes badly, I will count on around 650 kg per mu. That is how I will run the year: steady seed, steady fertilizer, enough water, and no waiting too long when work needs doing.
